featured.reason: NVIDIA's security scanner for agent skills and MCP servers: 71 patterns in 17 categories (prompt injection, exfiltration, supply chain, MCP tool poisoning, YARA, AST taint), optional LLM pass, 0-100 risk score and terminal/JSON/Markdown/SARIF output. Answers 'is this skill safe to install?' before you add one to Claude Code or Codex. Needs Python 3.12+ (or Docker); --no-llm runs fully static.
ideas: Run `skillspector scan --no-llm` over every skill already on your box (CLI-Anything, MoneyPrinterTurbo and the archived skill repos) and keep the JSON reports as a baseline before installing anything new.
Add a pre-install gate to your daily routine: scan each newly archived skill repo with `--format json` and show its 0-100 risk score next to the pick on ai-daily-radar.
Wire the SARIF output into a GitHub Actions job on a skills repo of your own so findings show up in GitHub code scanning on every PR.
Run `skillspector mcp` (MCP extra) so Claude Code or Codex can scan a skill from inside a session before you agree to install it.
Read its 17 categories (MCP tool poisoning, memory poisoning, trigger abuse) and use them as a checklist when you write your own SKILL.md files or MCP servers.
